The claim states that at a leaf node, the boundaries of the macro-cell are projected onto the image plane, yielding a hexagonal footprint. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'At a leaf node, the boundaries of the macro-cell are projected and rasterized onto the image plane yielding a hexagonal footprint.' This matches the claim exactly.

An iso-surface rendering algorithm based on object-order ray casting that subdivides data into macro-cells to build a min/max octree, reducing traversal steps by rasterizing hexagonal footprints [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the details provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly describes an iso-surface rendering algorithm based on object-order ray casting that subdivides data into macro-cells to build a min/max octree. It further states that at a leaf node, boundaries are projected to yield a hexagonal footprint, and for pixels in this hexagon, local rays are used to traverse the macro-cell grid, which reduces traversal steps. All specific technical details mentioned in the claim are present in the source text.
